english.title: During inquiry did something intended to prevent evidence / a document being given / produced / provided to inquiry
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), during the course of an inquiry, namely **(..SPECIFY INQUIRY..), did something, namely **(..SPECIFY THING DONE..), that was intended, or that you knew or believed was likely, to have the effect of preventing

(A)_[evidence]_
(B)_[a document]_
(C)_[documents]_
(D)_[**(..SPECIFY THING POTENTIALLY ALTERED OR DISTORTED..)]_

from being given, produced or provided to the inquiry panel
english.legislation: Contrary to section 35(2)(b) and (7) of the Inquiries Act 2005.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 35(4) of the Inquiries Act 2005 provides that "Aperson does not commit an offence under subsection (2) or (3) by doing anythingthat he is authorised or required to do (a) by the inquiry panel, or (b) byvirtue of section 22 or any privilege that applies.
(ii) Section 35(6) of the Inquiries Act 2005 provides that "Proceedingsfor an offence under subsection (2) or (3) may be instituted (a) in England andWales, only by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions; (b)in Northern Ireland, only by or with the consent of the Director of PublicProsecutions for Northern Ireland".
